findings.finding: workflow_agent is outside the envelope and profile revision, so two valid requests can share an attempt-fence and session; a paused one admitted its session before the fence lock and printed revision_not_admitted with dispatched:false although the other had dispatched, and the other could create its intent after that refusal.
findings.resolution: A first run reads the intent store under the per-work lock before any gate and admits its session under that lock after its fence record; another request's intent is substituted_request with dispatched:true and nothing admitted; every pre-intent refusal closes the attempt-fence before printing dispatched:false (fence-intent-creation-atomically task 3.2).

findings.finding: Two selected pairs under one envelope could both pin before either took the fence lock; the loser's intent creation failed on Error::State without abandoning its pin.
findings.resolution: Admission is single-flight under the lock, so the second request never pins; every path that ends before this run's intent, including a failed intent creation, abandons a pin this run made, never another run's (revision::abandon closes only a fresh pin; the failed-intent path cannot be reached under the lock and is checked by code inspection, not by a test).
tests: src/implementation_attempt/cli/tests/workflow_agent.rs::a_request_paused_while_another_dispatched_its_attempt_is_substituted_and_never_pins (exactly the first pair's pin is live while the second resumes; the second lifecycle is unchanged)

findings.finding: seam::effect, retained and close compared only the subject's definition, so a request naming an unselected revision got the pinned revision's permit and could close its pin.
findings.resolution: They compare the pin's or permit's revision with the request's subject: effect and retained are blocked and close is refused as session_conflict without closing.

findings.finding: admit-session called seam::admit without run's request validation, so it could pin a pair for a request that cannot run.
findings.resolution: admit-session applies Request::validate, the same function run applies, before seam::admit.
